column6: Own HIP decode runtime: the dense part on GPU 0 in exact fp8 kernels, routed experts on the CPU through ggml.
An exact AVX-512 kernel for the CPU's routed experts (fp4 weights x fp8 activations) instead of ggml's.
Routed experts split per layer: the routing study's most-used ones on the four GPUs, the rest on the CPU, all at once.
Expert-path fix 1: no GPU waits for the host between its expert lists.
Expert-path fix 2: a faster GPU kernel for a few experts per layer.
Expert-path fix 3: 16 CPU threads instead of 32 (32 starved the host thread); with fixes 1-2 the oracle bound went 16 -> 25 t/s.
Speculative decoding: the DSpark head drafts tokens and the main model verifies them; output identical to plain greedy.
Verification as one chunk forward: projections and the output head batched over the drafted tokens.
The routed experts batched over a verify chunk: one expert block for all its tokens.
A faster draft: its 5 positions go through each layer together (one weight read) and its head runs on the GPU, 26 -> 13 ms.
Hyper-connection kernels batched over a verify chunk (verify step 207 -> 181 ms).
A multi-token fp8 GEMV: one weight read for all of a chunk's tokens (verify step 181 -> 171 ms).
Draft length chosen per step from the draft head's confidence.
Placement-invariant expert numerics (--canon): the GPU's experts give the CPU's bits; its cost before the cache.
The adaptive expert cache: the GPUs keep recently used experts, swapped in the background; outputs unchanged.
Everything built with -O3: the CPU expert kernel had run 1.6x slower in the runtime at -O2.
Speculation measured live with the cache; a decode regression since step 37 (an engram copy per token) fixed.
The CPU kernel's preparation in parallel, and the cache tuned to 800 loads/s rebalanced every 8 tokens.
The router's top-k for all of a chunk's tokens in one launch.
One-token expert groups on the CPU's one-token routine.
The output head reads its several inputs through LDS.
Attention stage 1: the window kept as a ring of window + chunk slots.
Attention stage 2: the small per-token kernels once per chunk (measured before its commit, which also holds stage 3).
Attention stage 3: one attention launch for up to 8 tokens of a chunk.
The CPU's experts start right after routing: the other GPUs' copies are issued while the host is still ahead.
The engram rows read with pread (no page faults) while layer 0 runs, copied on their own stream.
The indexer skipped while it keeps every compressed position (up to 512): its scores were computed and dropped.
The CPU's activation digits written by one thread each (AVX-512): 16 writers had slowed every read of them.
The CPU's 32-row tasks handed out two at a time: each thread streams 64 contiguous rows before it jumps.
The CPU's rows copied to die 0 by a kernel: on the copy engine they had waited behind the cache's background loads.
The home die keeps its startup experts: the cache's loads into it had doubled half the drafts.
The verify step's argmax on the GPU: the host had copied all logits and scanned them.
The dies' results in smaller copies and the staged block in one: the copies had taken the worst-case size.
The compressor's projections read once per chunk: they had run once per token.
The attention output matrices' rows padded by 64 bytes on the GPU: rows a multiple of 4096 bytes apart had read at half speed.
Light launches that fill the GPU's 2048 wave slots exactly sent as two; the router's and compressor's rows padded.
